Its figures match the card and the tool outputs: 22.3% vs 4.2% expected, 5.4x, z 2.83, 16 of 22 below billed (73%), 19 of 45 charts below billed, 4 of 30 data-without-tests, and the unreliable estimate (7 charts in the 99215 stratum, 8 needed). The wording is cautious (\"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding\", the dollar estimate not quoted, no extrapolation from a targeted sample). The next steps are concrete. Several weaknesses keep it from a 5.","problems":["Cited claim C0025522 is described as a 28-year-old with 0 conditions and a moderate-MDM note. The claim's dx is J06.9, a minor URI billed at 99215, and the summary never says so. C0025510 is Z09 and has the same gap. Pointing out these diagnoses would make the low-complexity argument stronger.","The summary says \"A random sample was followed by a targeted 99215 sample, and both point the same way.\" The tool outputs only show two rounds, both labeled random. Nothing shown supports a targeted sample or the 'both point the same way' claim, so this is weakly grounded.","The second next step says to review the random sample in the recovery packet's sampling plan. That is vague and does not match the data seen. The stated dollar-estimate reliability issue is not turned into a concrete action, such as adding charts to the 99215 stratum.","Four of the six cited claims (C0025459, C0025492, C0025510, C0025522) have no documentation result. They only illustrate low-complexity patients, and the summary does not say that the supported 99215 claims with high MDM (C0025529, C0025531) are counterexamples. The rationale also omits that 42.6% of 99215s were low-complexity while other 99215s did go to high-complexity patients.","The summary does not flag the missing-results deficiency (MISSING_RESULTS) returned in both rounds, nor which items are missing. It says only that no audit trail was received.","The note-check line (problems 16%, late 4%, unsigned 0%, data 7%) is dense and unexplained, and the 'problems' term is unclear. The 'late' figure in the next step is stated as an issue even though 4% is small."]}
